faq.title: Still curious?
faq.description: Frequently asked questions from our users.

identify.q: Can I upload from my camera roll?
identify.a: Only after the animal has already been scanned. AnimalDex is built around real encounters first, then you can attach extra media from your camera roll to an existing capture.

family.q: How do you stop people from cheating?
family.a: We do not disclose the full system, but AnimalDex has anti-cheat checks in place to help protect real captures, collection value, and fair progression.

game.q: Is AnimalDex an animal identification app?
game.a: Yes. AnimalDex works as an animal scanner AI tool and identification app that helps with species and breed context, then keeps each sighting as a collectible entry.

respect.a: Yes. AnimalDex offers free credits when you start, you can then complete missions and earn more free credits. Paid plans are affordable and allow users to scan animals without limits.

rankings.introTitle: What is an animal tier list?
rankings.introParagraphOne: An animal tier list sorts species into bands instead of one score: S tier holds the standout animals, and the A, B, C and D tiers hold animals that fit the trait less and less. It is a more honest format than a single top 10, because it shows when several animals are effectively tied.
rankings.introParagraphTwo: Every AnimalDex tier list ranks 100 or more species on one trait — speed, strength, intelligence, danger, agility, adaptability and more — and explains the methodology behind the order. The quick answers below come straight from the same data as the full lists. Behind every animal is the same set of five AnimalDex stats, and a lesson you can use.

rankings.methodologyOverviewDescription: Different tier lists use different biological signals. Recorded speed, relative strength, body size, bite-force estimates, observed cognition, and documented risk are useful, but they are not directly interchangeable.
rankings.methodSpeed: Recorded speed is separated by movement context when air, land, and water performance are not comparable.
rankings.methodStrength: Relative strength considers body scale, force delivery, and real ecological use.
rankings.methodSize: Body mass, length, height, and practical field-guide scale can point to different answers.
rankings.methodBiteForce: Bite-force estimates are treated as category evidence, not as a universal danger score.
rankings.methodCognition: Observed cognition can include problem solving, communication, memory, and tool use.
rankings.methodRisk: Documented risk to humans depends on encounter context, region, and exposure.

statLessons.title: Every animal has five stats. Each one changes how you live its lesson.
statLessons.description: AnimalDex scores every species on speed, dominance, size, intelligence and rarity. The tier lists rank on them. The lessons read them.
statLessons.sectionDescription: The numbers behind every tier list, every battle and every card in your collection, and what each one says about the animal's lesson.
statLessons.recordedOne: When an animal is identified in the app, its species gets one canonical stat profile: five whole numbers from 0 to 100 for a typical healthy adult in the wild. An unremarkable species sits near the middle of each scale, not near zero, and reference species anchor every score so the order stays biologically honest: no fish outsizes a whale, no beetle out-dominates a bear.
statLessons.recordedTwo: Those base stats are the same for everyone. Your own capture can move away from them for real reasons, such as a zoo, farm or juvenile animal, but the species' numbers stay the species' numbers. They power the tier lists, battles and your collection, and they shape how each animal's lesson is meant to be lived.
statLessons.readsTitle: How a stat reads as a lesson

speed.name: Speed
speed.question: How fast should you move?
speed.recorded: How fast the animal moves when it matters: its sprint, flight, swim or strike, on one scale across every species.
speed.high: Act while the window is open. A fast animal's lesson rewards momentum: decide, move, and don't wait for perfect.
speed.low: Be calm about it. A slow animal's lesson is patience: a steady pace, no rush, and letting things come to you.

dominance.name: Dominance
dominance.question: How hard should you push?
dominance.recorded: How much the animal imposes itself: its strength, its weapons, and how readily it takes on rivals and predators.
dominance.high: Be brave. A dominant animal's lesson asks for courage, and for force or physical effort when the lesson calls for it.
dominance.low: Don't force it. A low-dominance animal wins by cooperation, timing or staying out of the fight.

size.name: Size
size.question: How big a step should you take?
size.recorded: Biological scale for a typical adult: mass, length and height, not how impressive it looks for its family.
size.high: Go all in. A big animal's lesson compounds: commit fully and let the weight build over time.
size.low: Step by step. A small animal's lesson works in small, repeated moves that add up.

intelligence.name: Intelligence
intelligence.question: How much should you think first?
intelligence.recorded: Observed problem solving, memory, learning, tool use and communication in the species.
intelligence.high: Think it through. A smart animal's lesson is mindful and mental: notice, plan, adjust.
intelligence.low: Trust the routine. Instinct and habit carry this lesson: repeat what works without overthinking it.

rarity.name: Rarity
rarity.question: When will the lesson show up?
rarity.recorded: How rarely you would meet the animal in the wild, from everyday species to the critically endangered.
rarity.high: Watch for the moment. A rare animal's lesson shows up rarely, at specific times. Recognise it when it comes.
rarity.low: Use it every day. A common animal's lesson is an everyday one, there in ordinary moments.

statLessons.listGenericDescription: This list isn't built on one of the five AnimalDex stats, but every animal on it still carries all five, and each one changes how its lesson is lived.
statLessons.listSeeAll: How AnimalDex records all five stats
statLessons.faqQuestion: What do AnimalDex animal stats mean for an animal's lesson?
statLessons.faqAnswer: Every AnimalDex animal has five stats from 0 to 100: speed, dominance, size, intelligence and rarity, and each one changes how its lesson is lived. A fast animal's lesson rewards acting quickly and a slow one's asks for calm. A dominant animal's asks for courage. A big animal's compounds, while a small one's works step by step. A smart animal's is mindful and planned. A rare animal's lesson shows up rarely, at specific moments.

locations.chooseGuideTitle: How to choose a local wildlife guide in {location}
locations.chooseGuideTipOne: Ask what they usually find in the season you are visiting. A good guide gives an honest answer, not a promised sighting.
locations.chooseGuideTipTwo: Check how they treat animals: no baiting, calling in, handling, or close flash photography for a better shot.
locations.chooseGuideTipThree: Confirm the meeting area, duration, group size, total price, and how you pay before the day, plus any permits or park fees the place requires.

descriptions.memory: Animals that survive by retaining routes, relationships, risks, and useful knowledge over time.
descriptions.observation: Animals that notice small changes, read their surroundings, and gather information before acting.
descriptions.teamwork: Animals that coordinate roles, share effort, and achieve more through cooperation.
descriptions.adaptability: Animals that change behavior, diet, timing, or habitat use when conditions shift.
descriptions.endurance: Animals that survive through pacing, sustained effort, and long-distance commitment.
descriptions.precision: Animals that notice small signals, aim carefully, and act at the right moment.

1.question: What are animal qualities?
1.answer: Animal qualities are simple strengths inspired by real animal behavior, such as teamwork, patience, precision, stealth, memory, and adaptation.

2.question: How does AnimalDex choose a quality for each animal?
2.answer: AnimalDex connects each quality to observable behavior, such as how an animal hunts, moves, communicates, protects itself, raises young, or adapts to its habitat.

3.question: Are animal qualities scientific facts?
3.answer: The animal behavior is grounded in real biology, while how you apply it to your own life is an interpretation inspired by that behavior.

4.question: What is an example of an animal quality?
4.answer: The elephant can represent memory because elephant groups rely on long-term knowledge, social bonds, and remembered routes to water and food.

5.question: How are qualities different from animal symbolism?
5.answer: Animal symbolism focuses on cultural meaning, while animal qualities focus on practical strengths drawn from observable animal behavior.

6.question: Can I use these qualities in daily life?
6.answer: Yes. Each quality includes a simple real-life application, such as using wolf-like teamwork for group projects or owl-like precision before making a decision.

anyPair.question: Can I compare any two animals?
anyPair.answer: Yes. Any two species in the AnimalDex catalog can be matched up — that is thousands of animals, so obscure pairings like a honey badger against a wolverine work just as well as lion versus tiger.

howItWorks.question: How does the comparison get written?
howItWorks.answer: Every matchup is built from the same species data behind the AnimalDex app: canonical size, speed, dominance and intelligence ratings, plus habitat and behaviour profiles. If nobody has run that pairing before, the breakdown is generated on the spot in under a minute and then published for everyone.

accuracy.question: How accurate is the winner?
accuracy.answer: Each verdict names a clear winner with a confidence score, and it is argued scenario by scenario — open ground, ambush, water, endurance — because the answer genuinely changes with the setting. Real encounters between wild animals are rare and situational, so treat the verdict as a well-reasoned read of the biology rather than a prediction.

missing.question: What if an animal is missing?
missing.answer: The picker only covers species indexed in AnimalDex. If a search returns nothing, that species has not been indexed yet — capture it in the app and it becomes available to compare.

wildProfile.title: Wild Profile
wildProfile.pageDescription: Your Origin, Apex and Active animals, found across the whole AnimalDex catalog.
wildProfile.interviewDescription: Your name and birthday for a first reading, then about ten questions about you. AnimalDex finds your Origin, Apex and Active animals across its whole catalog.
wildProfile.introBody: Wild Profile gets to know you. It starts with your name and birthday for a first reading, then asks about ten questions on things you may not have noticed about yourself. From what you say, it finds your Origin, Apex and Active animals across the whole AnimalDex catalog. Your profile syncs with the AnimalDex app.
wildProfile.inProgressBody: Your Wild Profile interview is in progress. Pick up where you left off here or in the AnimalDex app to reveal your Origin, Apex and Active animals.
wildProfile.privacyNote: Your answers are sent to AI providers (OpenAI, Google and Anthropic) to write your profile. What it learns is saved in “What I remember about you”, where you can see it and forget any of it. Resetting the interview deletes your answers.
wildProfile.goDeeperTitle: Your Wild Profile can go deeper now
wildProfile.goDeeperBody: The new interview starts with your name and birthday for a first reading, then asks about ten questions on things you may not have noticed about yourself, and searches the whole AnimalDex catalog for your animals.

interview.unavailable: Wild Profile is unavailable right now.

interview.introBody: First your name and birthday for a quick reading, then about ten questions on things you may not have noticed about yourself. AnimalDex then finds your animals across its whole catalog.

animalGroupChat.title: Talk to several animals
animalGroupChat.intro: Bring two or more of your animals into one conversation and hear how each sees it.
animalGroupChat.empty: Capture a few animals first, then bring them together here.
animalGroupChat.pickHint: Pick two to four of your animals, one of each kind. They'll talk it over together while you listen.
animalGroupChat.clearBody: This clears what you and your animals have said.
animalGroupChat.welcome: Ask them anything. They'll talk it over together, each in their own way, and tell you where they land. Pick one of them above to talk to it alone.
